'''Julyan Ray Stone''' (born December 7, 1988) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[UTEP Miners basketball|University of Texas at El Paso]].

==Early life==
Stone was born on December 7, 1988, in [[Alexandria, Virginia]] to David and Janet Stone. He has three siblings; his brother J.T. played [[college football]] at [[West Texas A&M University]], while his brother Jason played collegiately at [[San Diego State University]]. Stone attended [[Dos Pueblos High School]] in [[Goleta, California]], where he was a member of the varsity basketball team for four seasons. As a senior, he averaged 17 points, 8.0 [[Rebound (basketball)|rebounds]], 8.0 [[Assist (basketball)|assists]], and 5.7 [[Steal (basketball)|steals]]. After the season, he was considered a top 200 recruit by ''HOOP Scoop Online'' heading into college.<ref name="UTEP">{{cite web|title=Julyan Stone Bio|url=http://www.utepathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/stone_julyan00.html|work=utepathletics|access-date=December 26, 2011|archive-date=December 22, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111222175648/http://www.utepathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/stone_julyan00.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==College career==
Stone was rated as a two-star recruit by ''[[Rivals.com]]'' and was recruited by both the [[University of Texas at El Paso]] (UTEP) and the [[University of Portland]]. On May 4, 2007, he accepted the [[scholarship]] offer from UTEP.<ref>{{cite web|title=Julyan Stone|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/ncaa/basketball/recruiting/player-Julyan-Stone-66758|work=Rivals.com|publisher=Yahoo! Sports|access-date=December 26, 2011}}</ref> In his freshman season at UTEP, he averaged 2.8 points, 4.1 rebounds, 3.5 assists, and 1.6 steals, per game. He finished the season with 52 steals, second most on the team. He also finished with 114 assists and 50 turnovers, making his assist–to–turnover ratio 2.28, which was the best ratio for any freshman in all of college basketball that season.<ref name=UTEP />

As a sophomore, Stone finished the season with 5.6 points, 5.1 rebounds, and 1.4 steals per game. He also recorded 236 assists, which led the team and became the first player in [[UTEP Miners basketball|UTEP Miners']] history to record over 100 assists in both their freshman and sophomore seasons. Stone also became the leader in most double-figure assist games with six. During the post-season, he set a [[College Basketball Invitational]] record with 45 assists, recording eight against [[Nevada Wolf Pack men's basketball|Nevada]], 10 against [[Oregon State Beavers men's basketball|Oregon State]] in the first game between the two teams and then nine in game two against Oregon State.<ref name=UTEP />

During his junior season at UTEP, Stone averaged 6.1 points, 5.1 rebounds, 5.5 assists, and 1.6 steals per game. Against [[Arkansas State University]], he recorded ten points, seven rebounds, and eight assists, almost becoming the second player in UTEP history to record a [[triple-double]]. Against [[East Carolina Pirates men's basketball|East Carolina]], he recorded a season-high 11 assists. For the first time in his collegiate career, UTEP made it into the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA Tournament]]. In their only game of the tournament, Stone scored eight points, grabbed five rebounds, recorded seven assists, and stole the ball twice. The Miners wound up losing the game to the [[Butler Bulldogs men's basketball|Butler Bulldogs]], 77–59. Butler eventually made it all the way to the championship game against the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]], only to lose 61–59. Following the season, he was named to the [[Conference USA]] All–Defensive team.<ref name=UTEP />

As a senior, Stone finished the season averaging 8.5 points, 7.5 rebounds, 5.3 assists, and 1.5 steals per game.<ref name=stats>{{cite web|title=Julyan Stone State|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/julyan-stone-1.html|work=Sports-Reference.com|access-date=December 26, 2011}}</ref> In an article about the [[Legends Classic (basketball tournament)|Legends Classic]], a regular season tournament that UTEP participated in, ''[[Sports Illustrated]]'' writer [[Seth Davis]] commented that, "I also liked what I saw out of 6-7 senior point guard Julyan Stone, though I'm mystified as to why he has not developed more of an offensive game. If he did, he'd be a surefire pro."<ref>{{cite news|last=Davis|first=Seth|title=UConn's Walker is America's best player early on; plus more notes|url=https://www.si.com/more-sports/2010/11/29/kemba-walkeruconn|access-date=December 26, 2011|work=SI.com|date=November 29, 2010}}</ref>

On February 5, 2011, in a conference game against the [[Rice Owls]], Stone recorded a career-high 23 points, making seven of his nine shots and nine out of ten [[free throws]]. After the game, Rice head coach [[Ben Braun]] said that his team, "let Stone get to the rim and he made big plays."<ref>{{cite news|last=Duarte|first=Joseph|title=Rice falls short against Julyan Stone, UTEP 59-53|url=http://www.chron.com/sports/college-basketball-men/article/Rice-falls-short-against-Julyan-Stone-UTEP-59-53-1685192.php|access-date=December 26, 2011|work=Chron.com|date=February 5, 2011}}</ref> In his final career game at UTEP, Stone recorded one assist, which brought his career total to 714, the most in UTEP and Conference USA history by a single player.<ref>{{cite news|last=Albers|first=Fred|title=Miners Lose To Lobos|url=http://www.ktsm.com/sports/miners-lose-to-lobos|work=KTSM.com|access-date=December 27, 2011|date=March 15, 2011|archive-date=June 3, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120603202534/http://www.ktsm.com/sports/miners-lose-to-lobos|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was later named to the Conference USA All-Defensive team for a second straight season, as well as the Conference USA All-Conference second team.<ref name="stats" />

==Professional career==

===Denver Nuggets (2011–2013)===
Stone went undrafted in the [[2011 NBA draft]]. On December 9, 2011, Stone signed a two-year, $1.1 million contract with the [[Denver Nuggets]].<ref>{{cite news|author-link=Beau Bagley|last=Bagley|first=Beau|title=Former Miner Stone Signs Deal with Denver|url=http://www.ktsm.com/sports/former-miner-stone-signs-deal-with-denver|access-date=December 26, 2011|date=December 9, 2011|work=KTSM.com|archive-date=June 3, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120603202516/http://www.ktsm.com/sports/former-miner-stone-signs-deal-with-denver|url-status=dead}}</ref> During training camp, Stone was quoted as saying, "You got to go out there and give it your all on every possession. You can't have any bad days."<ref>{{cite news|last=Nelson |first=Dan |title=Dos Pueblos basketball star Julyan Stone could sign with NBA's Denver Nuggets for $1.1 million |url=http://thedailysound.com/2011/12/dos-pueblos-basketball-star-julyan-stone-could-sign-with-nbas-denver-nuggets-for-1-1-million/l |access-date=December 26, 2011 |date=December 19, 2011 |work=TheDailySound.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120202114232/http://thedailysound.com/2011/12/dos-pueblos-basketball-star-julyan-stone-could-sign-with-nbas-denver-nuggets-for-1-1-million/ |archive-date=February 2, 2012 }}</ref>

On January 3, 2012, Stone was assigned to the [[Idaho Stampede]] of the [[NBA Development League]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Denver Nuggets Assign Hamilton and Stone to NBA D-League Affiliate Idaho Energy|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=4337582|date=January 10, 2012|work=OurSportsCentral.com|access-date=September 25, 2015}}</ref> On January 10, 2012, he was recalled by the Nuggets.<ref>{{cite news|title=Nuggets Recall G Julyan Stone|url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/stone_recalled_01_10_2012.html|date=January 10, 2012|work=NBA.com|access-date=September 25, 2015}}</ref>

On January 30, 2013, Stone was assigned to the [[Iowa Energy]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Denver Nuggets Assign Julyan Stone to NBA D-League Affiliate Iowa Energy|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/denver_nuggets_assign_julyan_stone_iowa_energy_2013_01_30.html|date=January 30, 2013|work=NBA.com|access-date=September 25, 2015}}</ref> On February 13, 2013, he was recalled by the Nuggets.<ref>{{cite news|title=Denver Nuggets recall Miller, Stone from D-League|url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/denver-nuggets-recall-miller-stone-d-league|date=February 13, 2013|work=NBA.com|access-date=September 25, 2015}}</ref>

===Toronto Raptors (2013–2014)===
On September 19, 2013, Stone signed with the [[Toronto Raptors]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Toronto Raptors sign Chris Wright, Carlos Morais, Julyan Stone|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14278|access-date=September 25, 2015|work=InsideHoops.com|date=September 19, 2013}}</ref> On July 7, 2014, he was waived by the Raptors.<ref>{{cite news|title=Raptors Waive Julyan Stone|url=http://www.raptorshq.com/2014/7/7/5878531/raptors-waive-julyan-stone|access-date=September 25, 2015|work=RaptorsHQ.com|date=July 7, 2014}}</ref>

===Umana Reyer Venezia (2014–2015)===
On September 12, 2014, Stone signed with [[Reyer Venezia Mestre|Umana Reyer Venezia]] of Italy for the 2014–15 season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Umana Reyer Venezia signs Julyan Stone|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/134485/umana-reyer-venezia-signs-julyan-stone.html|access-date=September 25, 2015|work=Sportando.com|date=September 12, 2014}}</ref>

===Royal Halı Gaziantep (2015–2016)===
On September 25, 2015, Stone signed with the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]],<ref>{{cite news|title=Thunder Adds Stone, Wells and Zanna to Training Camp Roster|url=http://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release_trainingcamp_150925|access-date=September 25, 2015|work=NBA.com|date=September 25, 2015}}</ref> but was waived on October 22 after appearing in one preseason game.<ref>{{cite news|title=Thunder Waives Qualls, Stone, Wells and Zanna|url=http://www.nba.com/thunder/news/pressrelease_qualls_stone_wells_zanna_151022|access-date=October 22, 2015|work=NBA.com|date=October 22, 2015}}</ref> On October 27, Stone signed with [[Gaziantep Basketbol|Royal Halı Gaziantep]] of the [[Turkish Basketball Super League]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Gaziantep announces Julyan Stone|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/180010/gaziantep-announces-julyan-stone.html|access-date=October 29, 2015|work=Sportando.com|date=October 27, 2015}}</ref>

===Fort Wayne Mad Ants (2016–2017)===
On August 29, 2016, Stone signed with the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-sign-alex-poythress-and-julyan-stone|title=Pacers Sign Alex Poythress and Julyan Stone|work=NBA.com|date=August 29, 2016|access-date=August 29, 2016}}</ref> However, he was later waived by the Pacers on October 23 after appearing in five preseason games.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-waive-jeremy-evans-and-julyan-stone|title=Pacers Waive Jeremy Evans and Julyan Stone|work=NBA.com|date=October 23, 2016|access-date=October 23, 2016}}</ref> On October 31, he was acquired by the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]] of the [[NBA Development League]] as an affiliate player of the Pacers.<ref>{{cite web|first=Vinessa|last=Needham|url=http://fortwayne.dleague.nba.com/news/mad-ants-finalize-training-camp-roster-following-2016-draft/|title=Mad Ants Finalize Training Camp Roster Following 2016 Draft|work=NBA.com|date=October 31, 2016|access-date=November 1, 2016|archive-date=November 7, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161107015333/http://fortwayne.dleague.nba.com/news/mad-ants-finalize-training-camp-roster-following-2016-draft/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Return to Venezia (2017)===
On February 27, 2017, Stone signed with [[Reyer Venezia Mestre|Umana Reyer Venezia]], returning to the club for a second stint.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/227333/reyer-venezia-signs-julyan-stone.html|title=Reyer Venezia signs Julyan Stone|work=sportando.com|date=February 27, 2017|access-date=February 27, 2017}}</ref> On August 13, 2017, he parted ways with Venezia in order to return to the NBA.<ref>{{cite news|title=Reyer Venezia, Julyan Stone part ways. The guard will sign with the Hornets|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/244228/reyer-venezia-julyan-stone-part-ways-the-guard-will-sign-with-the-hornets.html|access-date=August 13, 2017|work=Sportando.com|date=August 13, 2017}}</ref>

===Charlotte Hornets (2017–2018)===
On August 23, 2017, Stone signed with the [[Charlotte Hornets]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Charlotte Hornets Sign Guard Julyan Stone|url=http://www.nba.com/hornets/press-releases/charlotte-hornets-sign-guard-julyan-stone|access-date=August 23, 2017|work=NBA.com|date=August 23, 2017}}</ref>

On July 8, 2018, Stone was traded to the [[Chicago Bulls]] in a three-team deal.<ref>{{cite news|title=Chicago completes trade with Charlotte and Orlando|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/chicago-completes-trade-charlotte-and-orlando|access-date=July 8, 2018|work=NBA.com|date=July 8, 2018}}</ref> On July 14, he was waived by the Bulls.<ref>{{cite web |title=BULLS SIGN JABARI PARKER |url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-sign-jabari-parker |website=NBA.com |access-date=July 15, 2018 |date=July 14, 2018}}</ref>

===Reyer Venezia (2018–2022)===
On July 25, 2018, Stone came back to Italy and signed a two-year deal with [[Reyer Venezia]] for the [[2018–19 LBA season|2018–19 season]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Julyan Stone Signs Deal With Reyer Venezia |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2018/07/julyan-stone-signs-deal-with-reyer-venezia.html |access-date=15 February 2025 |work=Hoops Rumors |date=July 21, 2018}}</ref> He averaged 4.5 points, 5.5 rebounds and 3.1 assists per game in the 2019–20 season. On June 16, 2020, Stone re-signed with the team.<ref>{{cite news |title=Julyan Stone re-signs with Reyer Venezia |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/julyan-stone-re-signs-with-reyer-venezia/ |website=Sportando |access-date=June 16, 2020 |date=June 16, 2020|last1=Skerletic |first1=Dario }}</ref> He re-signed with Reyer Venezia on July 10, 2021.<ref>{{cite news |title=Julyan Stone officially re-signs with Reyer Venezia |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/julyan-stone-officially-re-signs-with-reyer-venezia/ |website=Sportando |access-date=July 11, 2021 |date=July 10, 2021|last1=Maggi |first1=Alessandro }}</ref>

===Scafati Basket (2022–2023)===
On July 7, 2022, he has signed with [[Scafati Basket]] of the [[Lega Basket Serie A]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.scafatibasket.com/13875-2/|title=Altro Grande Colpo In Casa Givova Scafati: Firmato Julyan Stone|last=|first=|date=July 7, 2022|website=scafatibasket.com|publisher=|language=it|access-date=August 15, 2022}}</ref>

===Marinos B.B.C. (2024)===
On March 21, 2024, Stone signed with [[Marinos B.B.C.]] of the [[Superliga Profesional de Baloncesto]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Julyan Stone joins Marinos de Anzoategui |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/julyan-stone-joins-marinos-de-anzoategui/ |website=Sportando |access-date=March 21, 2024 |date=March 21, 2024}}</ref>
